added_models.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
engagement.note: NSF mice given human CD34+ cells carrying an alpha-Gal A lentivector raised plasma alpha-Gal A activity; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: While both experimental groups showed similar engraftment levels, only the therapeutic group displayed a significant increase in plasma α-gal A activity.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the NSF line's first use; vector was a sibling construct (LV-alpha-gal A/IRES/hCD25), so product_in_model false.

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT02800070 has no results posted (registry checked). Paired by us: Huang 2017 is the model side (LV/AGA-transduced patient CD34+ cells in NSF mice).
engagement.note: In FACTs (NCT02800070, LV/AGA, the vector later licensed as AVR-RD-01) all five men reached near-normal alpha-Gal A within a week, as the NSF xenograft predicted.
engagement.short: Patients made alpha-Gal A, as predicted
engagement.quote: All patients produced α-gal A to near normal levels within one week.
engagement.reason: Enzyme activity rose in all patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison; model and trial used the same LV/AGA construct, which is the voxeralgagene autotemcel lineage. Direction only, as mouse and human assays differ.

efficacy.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
efficacy.note: NSF xenograft predicted Gb3 clearance in kidney and heart; no patient trial yet.
efficacy.short: Xenograft cleared kidney and heart Gb3
efficacy.quote: Importantly, only in the therapeutically-transduced cohort was a significant Gb(3) reduction found in the heart and kidney, key target organs for the amelioration of Fabry disease in humans.

efficacy.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record: outcome typed PRIMARY in results; mean change -3.555 (range -4.020 to -3.090), only 2 analysed; trial terminated when AVROBIO dropped Fabry. Model side Huang 2017 abstract.

patient_trials.quote: reductions in plasma and urine globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) are seen.

efficacy.note: FAB-201 (AVR-RD-01): kidney PTC Gb3 inclusions fell by 3.6 per capillary at week 48 (n=2, registered primary), matching the xenograft's kidney Gb3 clearance.
efficacy.short: Kidney Gb3 inclusions fell, as predicted
efficacy.quote: Healthy renal tissue would have no Gb3 inclusions. A reduction from baseline is desirable.
efficacy.reason: Kidney Gb3 fell in two patients
efficacy.judgement: The results record lists kidney PTC Gb3 change as a primary outcome alongside AEs, so endpoint_role primary; n=2 keeps confidence medium.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.note: GLP-style toxicology in NSF mice xenotransplanted with the LV/AGA cell product found minimal untoward effects; supported the Health Canada CTA.
safety.quote: Additional toxicology studies employing NSF mice xenotransplanted with the therapeutic cell product demonstrated minimal untoward effects.
safety.judgement: Opening safety entry at the first public statement of the tox study; FACTs had started in 2016 but reported no safety data until 2021.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Confirmed later by NCT03454893 results (2024-01-05): no SAEs considered related to AVR-RD-01, no aberrant clonal expansion, no RCL.
safety.note: No serious adverse events attributable to the LV/AGA cell product in five patients; conditioning-related events only, as xenograft toxicology predicted.
safety.quote: No serious adverse events (AEs) are attributable to the investigational product.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison; xenograft silence on insertional or product toxicity held over follow-up so far. Conditioning (melphalan/busulfan) harms are outside the model.

added_models.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study

engagement.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study
engagement.note: ST-920 raised plasma and tissue alpha-Gal A several-fold above the earlier AAV2/6 vector in Fabry mice; STAAR patients not yet reported.
engagement.quote: Further optimization of vector design identified the clinical lead vector, ST-920, which produced several-fold higher plasma and tissue α-Gal A activity levels with a good safety profile.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the ST-920 product track; ST-920 had no track in the draft, whose gla-ko-mouse track is pegunigalsidase only.

engagement.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study
engagement.confidence_note: Registry results record (NCT04046224, posted 2026-04-14): mean change from baseline at week 52 ranged +14.7 to +162.6 nmol/h/mL across 9 dose/expansion groups (n=2-7 each). Paired by us.
engagement.note: In STAAR every ST-920 dose group raised plasma alpha-Gal A activity at weeks 24 and 52, as the mouse study predicted.
engagement.short: Patients' plasma alpha-Gal A rose, as predicted
engagement.quote: Change in alpha Gal-A activity in plasma from baseline at specific time points over the 1-year study period.
engagement.reason: Plasma enzyme rose in all dose groups
engagement.judgement: Mouse study ran before the 2019 trial start (IND-enabling), so prospective. Direction only; mouse and human assays differ.

safety.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no ST-920 NHP toxicology is public.
safety.note: The ST-920 mouse pharmacology/toxicology study reported a good safety profile; no patient safety results public yet.
safety.quote: Further optimization of vector design identified the clinical lead vector, ST-920, which produced several-fold higher plasma and tissue α-Gal A activity levels with a good safety profile.
safety.judgement: Opening safety entry for the ST-920 product track.

safety.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study
safety.confidence_note: Registry: serious TEAEs 3/33 (sepsis, brain stem stroke/CVA, chest pain, enthesopathy), none hepatic; non-serious transaminase/LFT rises in one female-group patient; related TEAEs common but none serious hepatic. Relatedness of SAEs not given.
safety.note: In STAAR (up to 2.63e13 vg/kg) no hepatic or other product-type serious harm appeared; SAEs were sepsis, stroke, chest pain and enthesopathy, as the clean mouse study predicted.
safety.short: No serious product-type harm, as predicted
safety.quote: All incidences of serious Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) in subjects who receive ST-920 as assessed by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE)
safety.reason: No serious hepatic harm in 33 patients
safety.judgement: Silence held: unlike FLT190 there was no serious transaminase event; the SAEs are Fabry-type or intercurrent events a mouse could not show. Medium because SAE relatedness is not posted.

Pegunigalsidase alfa population PK simulation of 2 mg/kg Q4W vs 1 mg/kg Q2W (BLA 761161 review Table 40): human model fitted to F20/F50 patient data, not a prospective preclinical system; FDA did not approve Q4W
FDA statement that Fabry-mouse lipid (primuline TLC) data could not confirm the clinical result: belongs to the existing gla-ko-mouse track, not a new system
Patient fibroblast/cell uptake and in-vitro neutralizing-antibody assays for pegunigalsidase: no comparison with patient outcomes found (PMRs only)
AAV5 alpha-galactosidase (Gla-KO mouse/NHP, 2024) and engineered alpha-Gal A AAV in aggravated Fabry mouse (2025): products outside the member list
In-vitro GLA mutant amenability assay (HEK293): validated for migalastat, a chaperone outside this class
ST-920 efficacy (STAAR eGFR slope, Sangamo topline press release, tier 5): the mouse study predicted tissue Gb3/lyso-Gb3, not renal function; no peer-reviewed or registry efficacy comparison to pair
